name: Pagination
purpose: Links that move between pages of a long list or table. It shows where the person is and lets them go back or forward.

notFor.when: The pages are different views, not slices of one list.
The pages are steps in a flow with a start and an end.

basis.source: registry/vois/pagination/pagination.tsx (shadcn plain markup, no Radix part)
basis.note: Behaviors come from the Notion UI SDK inventory (2026-11-21). The support tag on each one was checked against the source on the checked date. Pagination has no library behind it. The evidence is the Vois item file.

anatomy.note: A page link. It has no asChild.
The link to the previous page.
The link to the next page.

behaviors.text: Each page is a real link. Modifier clicks and a middle click open it in a new tab.
behaviors.note: A router link must be rendered by hand with the same classes, because PaginationLink has no asChild.

behaviors.text: Pressing the current page does nothing.
behaviors.note: PaginationLink only marks the active one. Skip the navigation in your own handler.

behaviors.text: Next on the last page and Previous on the first page are disabled.
behaviors.evidence: pagination.tsx: disabled sets aria-disabled, tabIndex -1 and a click handler that calls preventDefault
behaviors.note: A disabled link leaves the tab order, so keyboard users skip it.

behaviors.text: The bar works out its own page numbers from the total.
behaviors.note: Vois Pagination is plain markup. Do the count and the range in your own code.

behaviors.text: With many pages, the list shows the first, the last and a window around the current page, with an ellipsis for the gaps.
behaviors.note: The Ellipsis part only draws the dots. Choose the window in your own code.

behaviors.text: First and Last jump buttons are available.
behaviors.note: There are no PaginationFirst or PaginationLast parts. Add links with the same classes.

behaviors.text: Changing the page size resets to page one.
behaviors.note: Do this in your own page size handler.

behaviors.text: A page change can be refused, and the reason is reported.
behaviors.note: Nothing owns the page state. Check in your own handler before you navigate.

behaviors.text: Tab moves through the links in order. Enter follows the focused link.
behaviors.evidence: pagination.tsx: links are anchors, so the browser handles Tab and Enter

behaviors.text: After the page changes, focus goes to a sensible place, such as the top of the results.
behaviors.note: Move focus yourself, or the screen reader user does not hear that the list changed.

behaviors.evidence: pagination.tsx: isActive sets aria-current page and data-active
behaviors.note: Style it with the data-active attribute.

behaviors.text: The ellipsis is not read out as a page, and screen readers hear that more pages exist.
behaviors.evidence: pagination.tsx: PaginationEllipsis hides the dots with aria-hidden and adds sr-only More pages

behaviors.text: The bar is a navigation landmark with a label. Previous and Next have labels that say where they go.
behaviors.evidence: pagination.tsx: nav role navigation, aria-label pagination; links carry aria-label Go to previous page and Go to next page
behaviors.note: If a page has two paginations, give each its own label.

behaviors.text: The list keeps its list role, so screen readers announce the number of pages.
behaviors.evidence: registry/vois/pagination/pagination.tsx: PaginationContent sets role list on the ul
behaviors.note: The shadcn markup has no explicit role. vois-pagination adds it so the role does not depend on the CSS.

mistakes.text: Do not make the current page a plain span. It must stay a link with aria-current so screen readers can find it.
mistakes.evidence: pagination.tsx: isActive sets aria-current page on the anchor

mistakes.text: Do not use a disabled button for Previous on page one. Use the disabled link so the layout stays the same.
mistakes.evidence: pagination.tsx: disabled sets aria-disabled and tabIndex -1

mistakes.text: Do not use pagination for steps in a flow. Use a stepper.
